subject: could not define size of points in map plot

messages.author: ae88eae6775abfa2
messages.subject: could not define size of points in map plot
parts:
Hi, 
I am trying to show earthquake data on map but cannot define the size or alpha of the points.
I checked the help files and the website, could not find any sample codes.


The data file has been attached and the codes as following:

>require("maps") 
>require("ggplot2")
>test <- read.csv("test.csv")
>ggplot(test, aes(LONG,LAT))  + geom_point() + borders("nz")
..........works good.
>ggplot(test, aes(LONG,LAT,size=MAG, alpha=MAG,color="red"))  + geom_point()
..........works good.
>ggplot(test, aes(LONG,LAT,size=MAG, alpha=MAG,color="red"))  + geom_point() + borders("nz")
..........ooops. Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'MAG' not found


Thanks in advance.

Regards,
Simon

messages.author: 5196f936ff792c35
messages.subject: Re: could not define size of points in map plot
parts:
Simon, 

I'm not sure why it makes a difference, but I took some of the aes() from the ggplot() call and put it in geom_point() and it seemed to work. 

ggplot(test, aes(LONG,LAT))  + geom_point(aes(size=MAG, alpha=MAG), color="red") + borders("nz")

The only thing is that the area affected by the earthquake is small compared to the overall map. Perhaps it drives the point home enough? 

Brandon

Hi Brandon,

I could plot earthquake points on New Zealand map now according to Mr. Brandon's codes.   And subset the map borders with regions="South.Island".

>ggplot(test, aes(LONG,LAT))  + geom_point(aes(size=MAG, alpha=MAG), color="red")+ borders("nz", regions="South.Island", fill="gray")+ xlim(171.5,173.5) + ylim(-44,-42.8)

....  boders() just ignore the xlim and ylim parameters.

map() in mapdata package could show a subset of map easily.   But I like ggplot2.   I just wonder whether it is possible to show only a fraction of the map as borders in ggplot2.
Thanks in advance.

Regards,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: could not define size of points in map plot
parts:
Simon,
It appears as though you can use the map data from the mapdata package
in ggplot. After installing the mapdata package I just swapped the
names out and it looks just like your map (with a bit less green).

ggplot(test, aes(LONG,LAT))  +
borders("nzHires", regions="South Island", fill="gray")+
scale_x_continuous('Longitude',limits=c(171.5,173.5))+
scale_y_continuous('Latitude',limits=c(-44,-42.8))+
scale_size('Magnitude')+
scale_alpha('Magnitude')+
geom_point(aes(size=MAG, alpha=MAG), color="red")+

theme_bw()


With some tweaking you could get it to look better, but I still don't
know anything about how to fix the border edge problem.

Brandon

messages.subject: Re: could not define size of points in map plot
parts:
Hadley,

Indeed. I was going to ask why until I read the help file.

?coord_cartesian()

## Not run:
# There are two ways of zooming the plot display: with scales or
# with coordinate systems.  They work in two rather different ways.

(p <- qplot(disp, wt, data=mtcars) + geom_smooth())

# Setting the limits on a scale will throw away all data that's not
# inside these limits.  This is equivalent to plotting a subset of
# the original data
p + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(325, 500))

# Setting the limits on the coordinate system performs a visual zoom
# the data is unchanged, and we just view a small portion of the original
# plot.  See how the axis labels are the same as the original data, and
# the smooth continue past the points visible on this plot.
p + coord_cartesian(xlim = c(325, 500))

So it draws the whole thing filled in properly and then zooms in, which means you're not cutting the border in a funky way.

ggplot(test, aes(LONG,LAT))  +
borders("nzHires", regions="South Island", fill="gray")+

scale_x_continuous('Longitude')+
scale_y_continuous('Latitude')+

scale_size('Magnitude')+
scale_alpha('Magnitude')+
geom_point(aes(size=MAG, alpha=MAG), color="red")+

theme_bw()+
coord_cartesian(xlim=c(171.5,173.5), ylim=c(-44,-42.8))


It mucks with the axis breaks something fierce though. 

Brandon

Hi Brandon,

 

You can also use coord_map and play around with projections, etc ;)

fenrando

 

PS:

 

library("maps")

library("ggplot2")

library("mapdata")

library("gridExtra")
test <- read.csv("test.csv")
x11()

map("nzHires", regions="South Island", xlim=c(171.5,173.5), ylim=c(-44,-42.8), fill=TRUE, col="light green")

points(test$LAT ~ test$LONG)

####

 

p <- ggplot(test, aes(LONG,LAT))  +

 borders("nzHires", regions = "South Island", fill = I("slategray4")) +

 scale_size('Magnitude') +

 scale_alpha('Magnitude') +

 geom_point(aes(size = MAG, alpha = MAG), color = I("red")) +

 scale_x_continuous(name = 'Longitude', breaks = seq(from = 170, to = 173.5, by = 0.5)) +

 scale_y_continuous(name = 'Latitude', breaks = seq(from = -44, to = -43, by = 0.5))

 

p1 <- p +  coord_map(xlim = c(171.5, 173.5), ylim = c(-44, -42.8)) +  theme_bw()

p2 <- p +  coord_map(xlim = c(171.5, 173.5), ylim = c(-44, -42.8), orientation =  c(-90, 0, mean(range(x)))) +  theme_bw()

 

x11(14,6)

grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
